source.title: Transcriptomic analysis of spinal V1 interneurons informs their multifunctional role in motor output
source.citation: Trevisan AJ, Han K, Chapman PD, et al. Nat Commun. 2026;17:9614.
source.attribution: Trevisan et al., Nature Communications 17, 9614 (2026), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-76522-3. Article licensed CC BY 4.0. Atlas summary curated from article text and figures; no article images are redistributed.
source.reuseBoundary: The article is CC BY 4.0. This does not establish reuse rights for GEO files or other repository objects; those remain link-only and are not bundled.

study.populationScope: En1-lineage spinal V1 interneurons; one source-specific population, not a comprehensive spinal interneuron census
study.selectedNucleusUnit: V1 nuclei passing the source selection criteria across two replicates and four postnatal ages

clusterSizeRange.denominatorDescription: percent of the larger source V1 population; exact per-cluster nucleus counts are not imported

study.ageCoverageDescription: The article reports nuclei from P0, P14, P28 and P56 in each of the 14 clusters, in roughly equal proportions. These are cross-sectional samples, not longitudinal tracking of the same cells.
study.regionCoverageDescription: No cluster-by-region assignment is represented in this panel. Do not infer segment localization from a cluster label.
